Link the enclosure the host read (`housing.link`). Refused when a
link exists: relink it instead.

Apply what the host read of the linked enclosure.

Sent by `housing.update` and `housing.relink`: the references'
traces move the fixed geometry they own, bindings set their board
parameters, and the snapshot becomes the read. Refused, changing
nothing, when the board would not solve, or a bound parameter is
gone.

its trace enters the board sketch as fixed geometry it owns.

board-sketch dimension to it.

Bind a board parameter to an enclosure parameter the host read
(`housing.bind`), setting it to the value.

Stop setting a board parameter from the enclosure; it keeps its
value.

Forget the link. The geometry the references owned stays in the
board sketch as plain fixed geometry; the board keeps its shape.

publish_preview.description:
`interface.publish_preview` (a host request; reads only): the diff
against the last published revision and, when an enclosure is linked,
the dry run on a scratch copy of it (slices B3 and B4).

enclosure_path.description:
The linked enclosure's file: with it (and `path`, the design it
links), the preview runs the dry run on a scratch copy of it and
names the enclosure features that would move or fail (slice B4).

path.description:
The published `.solidcraft` design to compare with: the sidecar
beside it says where each datum was, so a moved datum reads by how
much. Without it, or when it is gone, a changed datum reads only as
changed.

tier.description:
The tier to preview; the last published one, or
[`Tier::Mechanical`], when omitted.

BoardFeatureId.description: Board-local cutout, slot or hole identity; never reused.

ContentHash.description:
A SHA-256 digest, written as 64 lower-case hex digits. Names a revision
record's canonical content (`library::bundle::content_hash`) or an
asset's bytes (`library::bundle::asset_hash`).

DatumGeometry.description:
A datum's geometry, in board millimetres. Profiles and volumes are
drawn in their frame's x–y plane; a volume rises along the frame's z.

loops.description: Closed loops, the outer one first, at most [`MAX_LOOPS`].

DatumId.description:
A datum's document identity, allocated from the table's own counter
([`InterfaceTable::next_datum`]), like nets from theirs, so exporting a
datum never shifts the ids of other objects. Never reused: the counter,
like the slot counter, only grows, through undo and redo too.

DatumKind.description:
The geometry a datum carries (docs/architecture/board-interface.md,
"Datum kinds").

oneOf.description: An origin and two axes: the board origin, a part's placement frame.
An origin and a normal: board top and bottom, a mating plane.

A point and a direction, with an optional diameter: a mounting
hole, an LED's light axis.

Closed loops of lines and arcs on a plane: the board outline, a
cutout, a connector opening's outline.

A profile and a height along its normal: a keepout, a part's
envelope, the space a plug needs.
A name, a value and a unit: board thickness, a board parameter.

DatumOwner.description:
The object a datum belongs to. Identity only: never a designator, a
name or a build order.

oneOf.description:
The board itself: its frame, faces, outline, thickness, parameters
and the tallest part per side.
A component placement, by instance id.
A mounting hole, by board hole id.

A cutout or slot of the board sketch, by the sketch curve that
starts its loop (the curve id of the lowest-ordered curve of the
loop; sketch curve ids are never reused).

DatumStatus.description:
Whether a datum's reference still resolves, in the outcomes RFC 0001
and the model-reference trace share.

oneOf.description: Exactly what was exported.
Found again, but by geometry rather than by name (a STEP face).

Its owner or feature is gone; the datum keeps its slot until it is
unexported.

Frame.description: An origin and two perpendicular unit axes; the third is `x × y`.

InterfaceSourceId.description:
A board's permanent identity in its published interface
(docs/architecture/board-interface.md): random, drawn once and kept
across every publish, so an enclosure can tell an older revision of
the same board from a different board. A deliberate slot
compaction draws a new one (a new epoch).

Written as 32 lower-case hex digits. The core never generates one:
`pcbcraft-io` draws them from the operating system and passes them
in as values.

Outline.description:
A closed exact outline in the pad frame: from `start`, each segment runs
to its `to`; the last must end at `start`. At most
[`MAX_OUTLINE_SEGMENTS`] segments. Flattening happens only for display
and checks, at an explicit tolerance.

oneOf.description:
A circular arc in bulge form: `bulge = tan(sweep / 4)`, positive
counter-clockwise; 0 is a straight line.

clearance_mm.description: The clearance a package datum asks for around an opening.

faces.description:
The carrier's faces by their role (`front`, `side`, `top`) and
their persistent names in the exported design.

hash.description: SHA-256 of this datum's canonical content, so a diff is per datum.

token.description:
Built from ids only (`i80.opening`); the name the enclosure's link
stores.

SketchCurveId.description: A SolidCraft sketch curve id (for example `l2`).

Slot.description:
A datum's position in the board's append-only slot table, from 0. The
exported design builds slots first and in slot order, so a slot's
feature ids, and with them its face names, follow from this number
alone. A slot is never reused: a removed datum's slot is retired.

Tier.description: How much of the board the exported design carries after the slots.

oneOf.description: The slots only.
The slots, the laminate, pads and parts (the default).
The slots and every copper body as well.

Vec3.description:
A point or a direction in board millimetres (x, y on the board's
frame, z up from the bottom face).

hash.description: SHA-256 of the canonical datum table.

revision.description: Counts publishes whose content hash differed, from 1.

unresolved_slots.description:
Live datums the design carries nothing for, ascending: lost ones,
and parameters whose value is an expression the core cannot
evaluate. Their slots keep their place, and an enclosure reference
to one fails until it resolves again.

AnchorName.description: An anchor authored by name in a part's model design.

AutoRule.description:
An automatic export rule. Every rule is on by default; each can be
switched off (`interface.auto`).

A housing reference (§7.2; slice S7).

BodyName.description: A body of a model design, by its name there.

BoxSide.description:
A side of an axis-aligned box in the part frame (before the placement
turns or mirrors it).

DatumKey.description:
What identifies a datum to the rules that make it: one key gives at
most one live datum. A feature datum's key has no name; its exported
feature tells it apart.

name.description:
The package datum's name (`DatumName` syntax), the board
parameter's name (`ParamName` syntax), or the side (`top`, `bottom`)
of a side height; `None` for every other role. Identity, unlike the
display name; `interface::check_key` holds the syntax per role.

The object a datum belongs to. Identity only: never a designator, a
name or a build order.

oneOf.description:
The board itself: its frame, faces, outline, thickness, parameters
and the tallest part per side.
A component placement, by instance id.
A mounting hole, by board hole id.

A cutout or slot of the board sketch, by the sketch curve that
starts its loop (the curve id of the lowest-ordered curve of the
loop; sketch curve ids are never reused).

DatumRole.description:
What a datum is to its owner (docs/architecture/board-interface.md,
"Roles"). The role and the owner decide the datum's kind, except for
[`Self::PartDatum`] and [`Self::Feature`], whose kind comes from their
source.

oneOf.description: An exported board parameter, named by the key's `name`.
A mounting hole's axis, with its diameter.
Courtyard × body height.

A datum the part's package revision declares, named by the key's
`name` (`part.opening` in the sidecar).

The tallest part on one side, the key's `name` being `top` or
`bottom`.

A feature the user exported: a part face, edge or vertex, a pad
centre, a board curve.
An automatic rule made it; switching the rule off retires it.
The user exported it (`interface.export`).

FaceName.description: A face's persistent name in a model design (`F2:side:l4`).

FeatureRef.description:
A feature of a placed part, rebuilt from the library
snapshot (or the part's model design) for every solve and never stored.

oneOf.description:
The placement origin (footprint datum), or a fill's or keepout's
outline start.
An axis of the target's frame through its origin.
A side of the courtyard's box in the part frame; `None`: its centre.
An anchor authored by name in the part's model design.

A face of the part's part file, by body, persistent face name and a
pick point on it (model frame, mm), traced in the board plane by the
host ([`ModelTrace`]). A name the part does not have is refused with
its faces square to the board, each by name with a point on it.
An edge of the part's 3D model.
An end of an edge of the part's 3D model.

The display name the user gave (`interface.rename`); `None` shows

PadPoint.description: Where on a pad a reference measures.

oneOf.description: A side of the pad's box in the part frame.

PartAxis.description: An axis of a part frame.

table.description:

next_datum.description:
The next [`DatumId`] to allocate, from 1 (0 until the first). Like
